tasks.short: Report authorised patient-health patterns to public health

steps.what: Read the public health agency's applicable reporting request or requirement and confirm the reporting period, case definitions, permitted patient data and the practitioner's reporting responsibility.

Retrieve the relevant recorded health conditions, disease status or births from the clinical record system {OTHER}; configure its native report filters and field export for the confirmed scope instead of repeatedly copying entries.

Check the selected records against source entries and case definitions, resolve duplicates and missing information, and determine the supported reportable health patterns without inferring unrecorded diagnoses or events.

Prepare the agency report with native field mapping and required-field checks in the clinical record system {OTHER}; check the completed final report's cases, counts, period, limitations, necessary identifiers and agency destination against the verified entries.
Save the checked final public health report and its source references in the clinical record system {OTHER}.
Submit the exact checked and stored public health report to the authorised agency through {GOV_PORTAL} and retain the submission reference.

tasks.design: Configure native report filters and agency-field mapping in the clinical record system {OTHER} before considering an integration. The practitioner verifies the cases and completed report, then saves it and submits the exact approved version through {GOV_PORTAL}; no model decides reportability or invents clinical events.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing clinical entries were repeatedly copied and rearranged into the agency's report structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reporting functions can reuse explicit fields and check required items against a versioned agency specification.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete records, ambiguous case definitions and scope of practice require human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a supported reportable event from an uncertain clinical entry and disclose limitations accurately.

ambition.what: No additional diagnostic, reporting or disclosure authority.

tasks.altitude: Less copying and formatting; the practitioner retains case selection and disclosure responsibility.

reach.learn: Clinical record provenance and agency schema versions.

evidence.claim: Native clinical reporting tools can filter existing record fields and populate a fixed reporting structure without determining clinical meaning.

assumptions: Boundary is reporting existing patient-health patterns where the practitioner already has an applicable duty or authorised request. It does not assume this occupation may diagnose or report every condition in every jurisdiction. Clinical care and the agency's processing are unchanged. Shares are illustrative, not observed.

Existing clinical record authors supply patient or case reference, event type, recorded status, event date, source entry ID and any agency-required demographic fields. The practitioner verifies period, case definition and source fields in s1-s3; unresolved data requires manual clarification or an explicit omission. Only fields required by the actual specification enter the report. Source collection and correction time are retained.

Native export and field mapping are tested first. If the record lacks a usable native report, manual entry remains the fallback and no saving is claimed for that case. No new recording, unreviewed free-text extraction or inference of births or diagnoses is introduced.

The normal author check at the end of s4 approves the completed report snapshot and agency destination for s5-s6. Any content or destination change invalidates both approvals. Submit time and ordinary receipt-reference capture are already in s6; no new approval meeting is added.
unknowns: Actual reporting responsibilities and permitted scope
Current native report functions and agency specification
Completeness of existing clinical event fields
research_questions: Can the existing clinical system map required fields while preserving each entry's source reference and missingness?

already_counted.description: Check native extraction and the completed mapped report, including disclosure scope.

incremental.description: Check agency schema changes and revalidate native report mappings.

approvals.approved_version: Completed final public health report and source references checked at the end of s4
Same final report snapshot and agency destination checked at the end of s4, unchanged by s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where copying and fixed report assembly remain manual, native extraction saves 12.5 hours and report mapping 12.6 hours per 100 baseline hours; 3 upkeep hours leave 22.1 net. Zero when already configured or the required fields cannot be exported. Case validation, save and submit retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The practitioner retains responsibility for supported clinical entries and authorised public health disclosure while native reporting reduces copying.
reach: Work with medical records specialists on source-linked event fields
role.ambitious_version: Provide only supported and authorised public health information with a traceable source for each reported entry.
